rawEvents.title: Wills, Trusts & Nursing Home Asset Protection
rawEvents.summary: ESTATE PLANNING WORKSHOP
rawEvents.description:
If you own a home or have assets worth at least $200,000; you owe it to yourself and your family to get the facts on living trusts as a part of an estate plan. If you think you are protected by a simple Will, think again. In many cases a Will guarantees your estate will go through probate, which means your family will not be able to take possession of your estate for many months or even years!

Plus a living trust may protect your assets if you become incapacitated during your lifetime by avoiding guardianship. This means your estate may be managed as you see fit, not as a court-appointed guardian sees fit

rawEvents.title: Shreveport, LA Martial Arts Program (Aikido)
rawEvents.summary: A welcoming Aikido program for ages 16+, focused on practical self-defense, balance, and stress reduction. No experience or uniform required. Try a free introductory class.
rawEvents.description:
Martial Arts for Real Life: Aikido in Shreveport

Our martial arts program offers a welcoming, adult-focused introduction to Aikido, a modern Japanese martial art centered on balance, connection, and effective self-defense. Designed for students ages 16 and up, this program emphasizes personal growth, physical conditioning, and practical movement skills in a supportive, non-competitive environment.

Aikido is often described as a martial art of harmony and control rather than brute force. Instead of meeting force with force, students learn how to blend with an opponent’s motion, redirect energy, and resolve conflict with efficiency and composure. Training focuses on throws, joint locks, pins, safe falling techniques, and situational awareness, skills that translate directly to confidence, coordination, and calm under pressure in everyday life.

This program is ideal for complete beginners as well as those with experience in other martial arts. No uniform, special gear, or prior training is required to start. Students are encouraged to attend a free introductory class to experience the practice firsthand, ask questions, and see whether the training environment is a good fit for their goals.

Classes are taught in a structured and approachable format, blending traditional martial arts principles with modern understanding of movement, injury prevention, and adult learning. Each session includes a warm-up, fundamental techniques, partner practice, and cool-down. Emphasis is placed on safety, mutual respect, and steady progress rather than competition or rank-chasing.

One of the defining features of this program is its inclusive, community-driven atmosphere. Students train cooperatively, supporting one another’s learning regardless of age, background, or fitness level. Aikido does not rely on strength, speed, or athleticism, making it accessible to a wide range of body types and experience levels. Progress comes through consistency, awareness, and refinement rather than aggression.

Beyond physical technique, students often find that training improves posture, balance, flexibility, stress management, and focus. Many practitioners report benefits that extend well beyond the mat, including increased confidence, better emotional regulation, and a greater sense of presence in daily life.

This program places strong emphasis on respect, accountability, and personal responsibility. Instruction is grounded in traditional martial arts etiquette while remaining practical and relevant to modern students. The goal is not only to teach techniques, but to foster resilience, discipline, and a mindset capable of handling conflict calmly and effectively.

Monthly enrollment options are available, with no long-term contracts required. Training is offered year-round, and students may join at any time. Periodic skill assessments and optional testing provide structure for those who wish to pursue formal rank, while remaining entirely optional for those training purely for fitness, self-defense, or personal development.

Whether you are looking to improve physical conditioning, learn practical self-defense skills, reduce stress, or explore a traditional martial art in a welcoming environment, this program offers a clear and accessible path forward.

New students are encouraged to reach out to schedule a free class, observe a session, or ask questions.

rawFeaturedEvents.title: New AHI Online Course on the Gilded Age and Progressivism
rawFeaturedEvents.summary: AHI's new online (via Zoom) on the Gilded Age and Progressivism led by Dr. David Frisk begins September 7. Reserve your spot by contacting  dfrisk@theahi.org or 202-999-5751.
rawFeaturedEvents.organiser_name: The Alexander Hamilton Institute for the Study of Western Civilization
rawFeaturedEvents.description:
AHI is pleased to announce a new online course for the fall of 2026. “America from 1868 to 1914: Prosperity, Progress, and Conflict.” Instructor: David Frisk, Ph.D.—AHI Resident Fellow. This course is free and open to the public. Advanced registration is required and AHI will reimburse participants upon the completion of a course should they be unable to afford required course reading. This online class will meet on Mondays via Zoom (link to be provided upon registration) from 7:00 p.m. to 9:00 p.m., September 14 through December 7. To sign up, or for more information, please contact Dr. Frisk at: dfrisk@theahi.org or (202) 999-5751. 

The late 19th century is often called the Gilded Age, a fascinating time of dramatic economic growth, impressive new wealth, industrialization, new social diversity, corruption, deep discontent, and upheaval both quiet and raucous. It was followed by a shorter but intense period of political and social reform—the Progressive Era. In these eras, best studied together because one grew out of the other, modern America was born. The main readings will be two highly acclaimed books by professional historians: American Colossus: The Triumph of Capitalism, 1865-1900 by H. W. Brands and The Search for Order, 1877-1920 by Robert H. Wiebe. The total assigned reading will be 25 to 30 pages per week. Each class session has a lecture-plus-discussion format, with time for discussion. There is a 10-minute break. Additional readings—mostly optional, but in several cases assigned—will be e-mailed to the class and will include such topics as:  Major business leaders, clashing economic visions, political machines, the Republican and Democratic parties of the time, growing immigration, labor strife and radical movements, fear of the many great changes brewing in America, new concepts in politics and government, reforms often stemming from the Progressive movement, and Theodore Roosevelt. In addition to three recent courses on the American Revolution, Dr. Frisk’s past AHI classes have examined subjects including Thomas Jefferson, Alexander Hamilton, The Federalist, other aspects of American constitutional history, Democracy in America by Alexis de Tocqueville, the Civil War, presidential power, the history and evolution of American political parties, the development of the idea of liberty, and conservative political philosophy. Dr. Frisk holds a Ph.D. in political science from Claremont Graduate University (2009), where he specialized in American politics and political philosophy. He is the author of the widely acclaimed If Not Us, Who? William Rusher, National Review, and the Conservative Movement (ISI Books, 2012) and is writing an intellectual biography of the legendary political scientist Willmoore Kendall.
